neighbours.label: the noun that closes a set prepositional phrase ('laid off from work', 'teeth in your mouth', 'faith in God', 'policy makers in government'), as against the same nouns used as modifiers or in other roles
fire: She was sent home from work with a high fever.
The dentist checked every tooth in my mouth.
He has kept his faith in God through many hard years.
The study was written for people in government and business.
Bury the bulbs deep in the ground before winter.
After the accident he took a month off from school.
Hold the lozenge in your mouth until it dissolves.
Their trust in God gave the sailors courage during the storm.
quiet: She left her work shoes by the front door.
The dentist said my mouth guard was too small.
He read a long book about the gods of ancient Greece.
The study was written for government officials and business leaders.
The ground floor of the house was flooded.
After the accident he missed a month of lessons.
Hold the lozenge still until it dissolves.
The sailors prayed for courage during the storm.
